items.q: The steroid regimen written is oral prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day (or 60 mg/m²/day) for 6 weeks with a maximum of 80 mg/day, followed by:
items.exp: Oral prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day (or) 60 mg/m²/day × 6 wks, max 80 mg/day → taper × 6 weeks → stop. (Book p759)

items.q: Remission (90-95%) is defined by urine albumin nil or trace for 3 consecutive days plus urine PCR below:
items.exp: Remission: urine albumin nil or trace × 3 consecutive days; urine PCR <200 mg/g. (Book p759)

items.q: The proportion labelled steroid resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) at this step is:
Which statement about nephrotic hyperlipidemia is TRUE as written?
opts: It resolves with steroid therapy, carries no atherosclerosis risk and has no role for statin
It persists despite remission and mandates statins
It raises atherosclerosis risk and needs statins
It resolves only after albumin infusion
items.exp: Resolves with steroid therapy; no risk of atherosclerosis; no role for statin. (Book p759)

items.q: Match each hyperlipidemia mechanism with its consequence — 1) ↑ lipoprotein lipase 2) ↓ lecithin cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) 3) ↑ VLDL, LDL synthesis by liver … A) ↑ VLDL, ↑ LDL, ↑ total cholesterol B) ↑ TG C) ↓ HDL
items.exp: ↑ lipoprotein lipase → ↑ TG; ↓ LCAT → ↓ HDL; ↑ hepatic VLDL/LDL synthesis → ↑ VLDL, ↑ LDL, ↑ total cholesterol. (Book p759)

items.q: The HDL fall in nephrotic hyperlipidemia is attributed to:
items.exp: D/t loss of HDL in urine: ↓ HDL. (Book p759)
